https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5yw.text: Image source, Getty Images By James Gregory Political reporter Published 10 August 2026 Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has proposed that all foreign prisoners are sent to serve their sentences abroad in order to scrap Labour's early release scheme. Farage said his party was exploring options with third countries over renting prison spaces, including El Salvador, which he said Reform chairman Lee Anderson would visit soon for initial talks. Reform said removing foreign nationals from the prison estate, as well as building emergency "Nightingale" prisons, would enable changes to be made to sentencing laws so that serious criminals serve out their full terms. Labour said the plan "does nothing" for the current situation as it would take years to arrange renting prison places overseas. Under Reform's plans, foreign criminals handed non-custodial sentences would be deported to their country of origin. Those with custodial sentences would serve all of it out in their home country, or a third country offering rented prison spaces if they refuse to take them. The party has previously suggested Kosovo and El Salvador as possible options, with Farage suggesting on Monday that Estonia and Lithuania could be looked at. There were 10,134 foreign nationals held in custody in England and Wales at the end of June, representing 12% of the total population. Reform claims its proposals for foreign prisoners would free up more than 10,000 prison spaces, but its policy document does not explain whether it would apply to remand prisoners awaiting trial, which make up around a third of that number. Both Farage and home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf did not address this point when asked to do so at a press conference to unveil the plans on Monday. 'Half the cost' Last year, Farage said El Salvador was an "extreme example" of a country where the party could send foreign prisoners. On Monday, he played down accusations of human rights abuses in the Central American country, saying: "Not all of the prisons are cages." El Salvador has the highest incarceration rate in the world, following a government crackdown on gang-related crime, and is home to the notorious mega-jail, the Center for the Confinement of Terrorism (Cecot). Reform says an agreement would require El Salvador to adhere to "British standards on size, lighting, heating, ventilation and fittings, and require daily open air time". Farage added: "To house a foreign national offender in El Salvador will be half the cost of housing a foreign national offender in this country, and will give us more prison spaces." The party said on completion of their sentence, foreign national offenders would return to their home country and be barred from re-entering the UK. The party has not set out a budget for this scheme, saying instead that deals to send prisoners abroad would save on the "billions of pounds" it currently costs the government to house them in the UK. Other countries have pursued similar arrangements - in 2021, Denmark agreed to pay Kosovo an annual fee of Â£12.8m for an initial five-year period to rent 300 of their prison spaces. Prisoner release row proving to be Burnham's first big test as PM Published 7 August It comes as the government comes under increasing pressure over its early release scheme, which is now due to start in October in England and Wales when the first batch of a total 5,000 prisoners are due to be released. Last week, Andy Burnham announced that prisoners convicted of rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences would be excluded from the scheme, adding that he wanted to exclude more but prison overcrowding prevented this. Two of PC Andrew Harper's killers, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, remain eligible to be freed halfway through their 13-year sentences after they were convicted of manslaughter in 2020. On Monday, Downing Street said it was "not possible" to exempt "one or two offenders" convicted of manslaughter from early release. Farage said that "Labour have inherited a very, very difficult situation" from the Conservatives, but added: "They don't appear to have the imagination or the will to solve it." Deportation automatically applies to foreign nationals who are sentenced to at least 12 months in prison, though there is an appeals process. The UK returned 5,858 foreign national offenders in the year ending March 2026, up 13% on the previous year and the highest observed since 2017, according to the latest Home Office figures. , external A further 15 countries were added to the Home Office's "deport now, appeal later" scheme last year , allowing the government to send foreigners who commit crimes in the UK back to their home countries before they can appeal the decision. 'Free for all' As well as freeing up places, Yusuf said: "There will be a lot more people in prison under a Reform government." He added that "killers, rapists and thugs will never be released a day early". The party claims that its proposed law changes, including reinstating short sentences for shoplifters and ensuring serious offenders serve out their full terms, would increase the prison population by 18,000. This would be covered by the 22,000 places made available under Reform's deportation and Nightingale plans, the party says. Reform UK has pledged to build 12,400 new places in Nightingale prisons on Ministry of Defence land within 18 months of forming a government, at a cost of Â£5bn over the next Parliament. The Nightingale label is a reference to the network of emergency temporary hospitals set up during the Covid pandemic. The prison population in England and Wales on 3 August was 86,495, which was 97% of useable capacity. The Ministry of Justice has warned the prison population will overtake capacity as soon as this November. Labour said Reform's proposal was not a "serious prison plan", adding: "Nigel Farage knows full well that renting prison places overseas would take years to arrange and does nothing to tackle the pressures we face now." A spokesperson for the party said Labour was building 14,000 additional places and had removed 10,000 foreign criminals since the 2024 election, up 36% on the previous 21 months. A man can have no greater love than to lay down his life for his friends. You are my friends, if you do what I command you. I shall not call you servants any more, because a servant does not know his master's business; I call you friends, because I have made known to you everything I have learnt from my Father. You did not choose me: no, I chose you; and I commissioned you to go out and to bear fruit, fruit that will last; and then the Father will give you anything you ask him in my name.' Reflection on the painting The story of Saint Maximilian Kolbe, whose feast we celebrate today, stands as one of the most heroic testimonies of the Second World War. In Auschwitz, when ten prisoners were selected to die by starvation in reprisal for the apparent escape of another inmate, one of them, Franciszek Gajowniczek, cried out in anguish for his wife and children. Kolbe stepped forward and calmly offered to take his place. He had no way of knowing whether Gajowniczek would survive the camp or ever see his family again. There was no guarantee that his sacrifice would lead to a happy ending; Kolbe simply recognised another man's suffering and chose to give his own life so that he might have the possibility of living. Remarkably, Gajowniczek did survive. After more than five years in concentration camps, he was liberated and reunited with his wife. Tragically, however, their two sons had been killed shortly before the war ended. He lived until 1995 and spent much of his later life bearing witness to the priest who had died in his place, attending both Kolbe's beatification in 1971 and his canonisation in 1982. Kolbe's story recalls the words of Jesus: 'The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.' Christ himself faced death at only thirty-three, yet freely embraced the Cross so that others might live. Kolbe followed his Lord along that same path of self-giving love. Saint Maximilian Kolbe, born Raymund Kolbe, was a Polish Conventual Franciscan friar and priest with a profound devotion to the Immaculate Virgin Mary. During the German occupation of Poland, he remained at the monastery of Niepokalanów, where the friars sheltered and supported thousands of displaced people, including many Jews. Through his widely circulated publication, The Knight of the Immaculate, Kolbe also resisted the hatred and falsehoods of Nazi ideology. He was arrested by the Gestapo in February 1941 and eventually deported to Auschwitz. Whilst Kolbe endured the starvation bunker for nearly two weeks, encouraging the condemned men through prayer and hymns, he was the last surviving one of the group. Eventually the guards killed him with an injection of carbolic acid on 14 August 1941, the eve of the Assumption. I will leave you with the words of a letter which he wrote on 15 June 1941 to his mother, telling her not to worry about him: "Dear Mama, At the end of the month of May I was transferred to the camp of Auschwitz. Everything is well in my regard. Be tranquil about me and about my health, because the good God is everywhere and provides for everything with love. It would be well that you do not write to me until you will have received other news from me, because I do not know how long I will stay here. Cordial greetings and kisses, affectionately. Raymund." ...two months later Maximilian died. Our striking painting by the American artist Neilson Carlin portrays Saint Maximilian Kolbe as an emaciated figure within the horrors of Auschwitz. His face bears the marks of suffering, yet radiates remarkable serenity and compassion. Most striking of all is the halo fashioned from twisted barbed wire... a powerful symbol that transforms an instrument of cruelty into a sign of sanctity. Saint Maximilian Kolbe. Pray for us. https://www.wkyufm.org/news/2026-08-17/f.text: On Air Now Playing 88.9 Bowling Green | 89.5 Owensboro | 89.7 Somerset | 90.9 Elizabethtown On Air Now Playing WKU Classical News Fall '26 WKU students arriving at campus in transition WKU Public Radio | By Lisa Autry Published August 17, 2026 at 4:47 PM CDT Twitter LinkedIn Email Katie Corbin President Timothy C. Caboni presented the Spirit of WKU Award to Dr. Corinne Murphy. Western Kentucky University students arriving for the upcoming fall semester are seeing a campus in transition. In his annual opening convocation to faculty and staff on Monday, President Timothy Caboni highlighted the challenges of having three of the school’s newest residence halls shuttered due to faulty construction. Two of those dormitories, however, have reopened. Students are currently moving into Normal and Regents Halls, which make up part of the First-Year Village. Demolition is nearly complete on Douglas Keen and Hugh Poland Halls, making way for the Southern Gateway project. The 1,000-bed dormitory will open in Fall 2028 with private rooms and suite-style living, essentially doubling the number of Living Learning Communities on campus. “It’s going to be two years of construction that our campus community will have to navigate, but the outcome on the other side of that is going to be transformational for our university," Caboni said. “I think it’s important for us that we’ll be able to use that as a recruitment tool." Another new residence hall will be built close to where Hilltopper Hall stood and will replace the aging Gilbert Hall, McCormack Hall and Rodes Harlin Hall. Hilltopper Hall was razed over the summer after it was determined that repairs on the structure would be too costly. WKU has a housing occupancy rate this fall of 93% with Normal and Regents Halls back online. The university has accommodated other displaced students by converting the Hyatt Place hotel into a residence hall and utilizing space in the Campus Flats apartments. Following the housing debacle, WKU signed an agreement with real estate company Gilbane , which takes over construction and management of WKU dorms from the Student Life Foundation. “I know there were questions around this new partnership. I think we have all felt the difference in terms of the cleanliness of the facilities, but also the attention and care given to preparation," Caboni told reporters following his address. "We are in a much better place to welcome students this year than we were last year.” In other campus construction updates, the renovation of Cherry Hall continues with plans to reopen the historic building in the fall of 2027. A building that will replace the Academic Complex is scheduled to open in Fall 2029. The convocation concluded with the annual Spirit of WKU Award. This year’s recipient was Dr. Corinne Murphy, dean of the College of Education and Behavioral Sciences. The full text of the convocation can be found here. Tags News Western Kentucky Univeristy WKU Twitter LinkedIn Email Lisa Autry Lisa is a Scottsville native and WKU alum. She has worked in radio as a news reporter and anchor for 18 years. Prior to joining WKU Public Radio, she most recently worked at WHAS in Louisville and WLAC in Nashville. She has received numerous awards from the Associated Press, including Best Reporter in Kentucky. Many of her stories have been heard on NPR. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: Smoke rises over Kyiv after Russian strikes Ukraine Ukrainian soldiers in combat have access to Starlink satellite internet restricted Outage of terminals managed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX comes as Russia launches ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from US Andrew Roth in Kyiv Wed 14 Oct 2026 06.05 EDT First published on Wed 14 Oct 2026 04.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukrainian soldiers in combat have suddenly had their access to Starlink satellite internet terminals restricted as the Trump administration has increased pressure on Ukraine to halt long-range strikes on Russia’s oil industry immediately. The terminals, which are distributed and managed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations and the sudden restrictions on the terminals travelling at high speeds on Tuesday evening led to the failure of several combat missions, said an adviser on military technology to Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy . The sudden outage came as Russia launched ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from the US for a second night. For years, the US has provided Ukraine with intelligence when strikes were about to take place. Donald Trump has denied that his administration has cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine . Zelenskyy also indicated that the US was continuing to share intelligence with Ukraine in an interview with NPR aired on Wednesday, but confirmed that military advisers had received threats from the US that intelligence sharing could be limited. Ukraine did not receive any warning before Russia launched its first barrage of ballistic missiles on Tuesday evening, according to Col Yurii Ihnat, a spokesperson for the air force. But it did receive warnings from “foreign partners” about three subsequent barrages, leaving further confusion about whether or not the US is intentionally withholding intelligence from Ukraine. SpaceX did not confirm any changes to Starlink’s functionality and it was not immediately clear why the restrictions had been put in place. Terminals travelling at more than 100mph and using a version of Starlink for the military and other national security agencies suddenly lost connectivity, said Serhiy Beskrestnov, in what appeared to be a targeted outage meant to disrupt military operations. “Our armed forces did not receive a warning about these restrictions and this led to the failure of a number of missions,” said Beskrestnov, who is also a popular military blogger. “It’s clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is connected to the current political situation.” Limiting Starlink’s access speeds would have a significant effect on Ukraine’s mid-range strike campaign, where it uses the satellite internet system to navigate drones to hit targets behind the front in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. But there have been no reports that access for static Starlink terminals have been cut, meaning critical battlefield communications for soldiers should remain unaffected. The detection of incoming Russian missiles and drones relies on other technologies. Musk, an ally of Trump, had previously cut off Starlink service to Ukrainian soldiers during an offensive that took a small amount of Russian territory. Serhii Sternenko, a political activist with close ties to the military, first reported the outage and later said that the speeds at which the loss of connectivity occurred had fallen even lower. “It is likely that the company ‘SpaceX’ resorted to such measures at the request of the Trump administration,” he said. “Ordinary satellite communication terminals are currently operational.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy decries ‘absolutely unjust’ lack of warning from allies after Kyiv plant strike Read more Trump has demanded that Ukraine stop striking Russian oil refineries, which he has blamed for the high cost of diesel, although most analysts say that the closure of the strait of Hormuz has had a far larger impact on global energy prices. Zelenskyy had suggested, though not said, that the US was intentionally withholding intelligence from Ukraine about impending Russian missile strikes. Russia carried out a massive strike against Ukrainian energy infrastructure late on Tuesday evening, Zelenskyy said, launching 39 ballistic missiles and 120 attack drones against Kyiv and Kharkiv. The strikes hit several power plants and key substations that carry electricity to the capital, including from a major power plant. “The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale – Russia has never before shown such ostentatious disrespect toward the United States,” he said. “Russia does not consider the American president’s statements strong.” At least 600,000 people were now without power, he said, adding that outages could become even more widespread. https://www.mediafax.ro/english/what-luc.text: What Luca Niculescu wants for the foundation of the Governments’s Agenda Luca Niculescu: Reforms must be made „for the people” Prime Minister-designate Luca Niculescu said on Tuesday that the experience gained over the last four years, during which he coordinated Romania’s accession process to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), should be used in the construction of the future governing program. „In the last four years, I have coordinated the process of Romania’s accession to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). It was the most intense professional experience I have ever had and an extraordinary X-ray of the Romanian state: the economy, administration, education, health, state-owned companies, labor market, taxation,” Niculescu posted on Facebook . According to him, one of the main lessons of this period is that reforms must be built on concrete data and reality on the ground. „I have learned one important thing in these years: good reforms are made based on data, reality on the ground, and other successful experiences. And they are made for the people,” added the prime minister-designate. Over 100 reforms in the OECD accession process Luca Niculescu claims that the OECD accession process has already generated over 100 reforms in Romania and states that these should be continued and integrated into the future government program. „I want this work to continue and become one of the foundations of the governing program. Not because the OECD recommends it, but because they are good ideas for Romania, evaluated and tested in some of the world’s best-performing economies,” he said. The designated Prime Minister also insisted on the political consensus that has existed so far around Romania’s accession to the OECD. Call for consensus between parties Luca Niculescu showed that the parties have succeeded, in recent years, in jointly supporting the objective of joining the OECD, despite political differences. „The political parties managed to jointly support an important objective for Romania, beyond the natural differences between them. This consensus mattered enormously,” he said. Niculescu expresses hope that the same approach can be maintained in the negotiations for the future Government. „I hope we find the same openness now, around a realistic program, built on what unites us. I am open to discussions and respect good ideas, regardless of where they come from,” concluded the prime minister-designate. Nicușor Dan’s fourth nomination Luca Niculescu was appointed by the head of state on Monday, October 5, after consultations with the parliamentary parties and political formations at the Cotroceni Palace. This is the fourth nomination for the position of prime minister made by Nicușor Dan. The president signed the decree on Tuesday regarding the appointment of Luca-Alexandru Niculescu as a candidate for the position of prime minister.
